name: reviewer-dev-via-test decide(rejected_retry) → stamp retry markers on run entity
description:
ADR-044 §addendum Slice 5 — CBG dev-fixable bounded retry, stamp half. Fires when CBG (reviewer-dev-via-test) decides rejected_retry: the integration gate failed (or the diff showed a constraint violation) AND CBG judged it a bounded implementation fix Ralph can do WITHIN the existing plan (not a plan/scope/human problem — that's bare `rejected` → rule 07b). CBG names the offending task in decide.subtopics=[<task-id>] and the concrete fix in decide.reason.

This rule fires on the CBG loop entity (fresh each pass) and writes three markers onto the RUN entity (the original coordinator loop, via lineage.run-loop-entity-id subject override — same #147/#148 pattern as autoresearch rule 04a):

- dev_via_test.cbg.retry.target_task (update_triple, upsert) = CBG's subtopics — which task to re-dispatch. Upsert so only the latest CBG verdict's target survives across passes.
- dev_via_test.cbg.retry.finding (update_triple, upsert) = CBG's reason — the concrete fix Ralph must apply, read by the retry-Ralph as an added acceptance constraint and surfaced to the coordinator.
- dev_via_test.cbg.retry.pending (add_triple) = this CBG loop id — the presence marker that triggers the run-entity driver (rule 07d). add_triple (not update) because 07d removes it each cycle; the remove-then-re-add across passes is the canonical semstreams#204 presence-marker discipline.

Why two rules (07c stamp + 07d driver): the retry BUDGET is bounded by $state.iteration, which is a per-(rule, entity) transition counter that resets on a fresh entity. CBG loops are fresh each pass, so the counting rule MUST anchor to the stable run entity. 07c (CBG entity) only stamps; 07d (run entity) does the bounded routing where $state.iteration is the stable retry counter. See ADR-044 §addendum Slice 5 'The bound is structural'.

metadata.subject_override_requires: semstreams #147/#148 (resolveTripleSubject shared by add/update/remove_triple). CBG carries lineage.run-loop-entity-id from rule 06's related_loops.
metadata.upsert_rationale: target_task + finding use update_triple (remove-then-add upsert) so the latest CBG verdict overwrites the prior one — a stale finding from retry N must not leak into retry N+1. pending uses add_triple because it is a content-free trigger that 07d removes each cycle.
metadata.verdict_split: CBG action_allowlist (rule 06) is [approved, rejected_retry, rejected]. approved → 07a (respond_direct). rejected_retry → 07c (this rule, bounded re-dispatch). rejected → 07b (ask_user, the fail-safe default for plan/scope/human problems). Bare `rejected` keeps its existing 07b binding so an under-specified CBG escalates rather than silently looping.
metadata.subtopics_fence: The subtopics length_gt 0 condition is a STRUCTURAL guard (go-reviewer C1, ADR-044 §addendum Slice 5). The decide tool stamps coordinator.decision.subtopics ONLY when non-empty (semstreams decide.go), and there is no unresolved-token guard on add/update_triple OBJECTS (only on subjects). Without this fence, a rejected_retry emitted WITHOUT subtopics would stamp target_task = the literal string '$entity.triple.coordinator.decision.subtopics' (garbage), silently mis-targeting the retry. With the fence, a subtopics-less rejected_retry does NOT fire this rule — rule 07e catches it and escalates to ask_user (fail-safe, mirrors rule 01's length_eq 0 corruption-to-no-op fence). Per [[encode-principles-structurally]]: the persona prose 'name exactly one task id' is hopeful; this fence is enforcement.
